title: The Decision Process
summary: We talked about big decisions in our lives and whether we regret them. We practised the third conditional and 'I wish + past perfect' to talk about the past, time linkers for telling our life story, and weak forms like 'would've'.

grammar.title: Third conditional
grammar.explain: We use the third conditional to imagine a different past. The situation is finished and we can't change it. We often use it to talk about regrets. Use 'might have' when you are not sure about the result.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم الحالة الشرطية الثالثة لتخيّل ماضٍ مختلف عمّا حدث. الموقف انتهى ولا يمكن تغييره، ونستخدمها كثيراً للتعبير عن الندم. نستخدم might have عندما لا نكون متأكدين من النتيجة.
form: If + had + past participle, would have + past participle
If + had + past participle, might have + past participle (= maybe)
would have + past participle + if + had + past participle

examples.en: I wouldn't have made the same decision if I had known.
If I hadn't left the UK, I might have married Claire.
examples.note: Wilson left the UK. Maybe he would have married Claire.

examples.en: I still would've done the same thing.
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
examples.note: I didn't study hard, so I failed.

mistakes.wrong: If I would have known, I would have helped.
mistakes.right: If I had known, I would have helped.

mistakes.wrong: If I had left earlier, I would caught the bus.
mistakes.right: If I had left earlier, I would have caught the bus.
mistakes.why: The result needs 'would have' + past participle.

mistakes.wrong: If I hadn't leave my hometown...
mistakes.right: If I hadn't left my hometown...

mistakes.wrong: I would have went on holiday.
mistakes.right: I would have gone on holiday.
mistakes.why: Use the past participle (gone), not the past simple (went).

quiz.q: If she ___ earlier, she wouldn't have missed the bus.
If I had known about the party, I ___ .
If I hadn't moved to Cairo, I ___ met my wife.
quiz.why: might not have + past participle = maybe not.

quiz.q: 'I still would've done the same thing.' Does the speaker regret it?
quiz.why: 'Still' shows she is happy with her choice.

quiz.q: I wouldn't have got sick if I ___ the tap water.

options: If he had asked me, I would have helped.
If he would have asked me, I would have helped.
If he asked me, I would have help.
quiz.why: had + past participle in the if-part, would have + past participle in the result.

grammar.title: Talking about regrets: I wish / If only / should have / regret + -ing
grammar.explain: We use these forms to say we are sorry about the past. 'I wish' and 'If only' + past perfect talk about past things we can't change. 'If only' is stronger.
grammar.explain_ar: نستخدم هذه التراكيب لنقول إننا نادمون على شيء في الماضي. I wish و If only مع الماضي التام تتحدث عن أشياء في الماضي لا يمكن تغييرها، و If only أقوى في التعبير. ونستخدم should have للوم أنفسنا، و regret مع ‎-ing للندم المباشر.
form: I wish + past perfect (I wish I hadn't left school so early.)
If only + past perfect (If only I had listened!)
should have + past participle (I should have called her.)
regret + verb-ing (I regret leaving my job.)
I wish + past simple = present regret (I wish I had more time.)

examples.en: I wish I hadn't left school so early.
examples.note: Grace left school early and now she is sorry.

examples.en: If only I had listened to my teacher!
I should have booked the hotel earlier.
examples.note: I didn't book early, and that was a mistake.

examples.en: I regret leaving my old company.

mistakes.wrong: I wish I didn't leave school.
mistakes.right: I wish I hadn't left school.
mistakes.why: For the past, use wish + past perfect.

mistakes.wrong: I regret to leave my job last year.
mistakes.right: I regret leaving my job last year.

mistakes.why: 'Regret' is a normal verb, so the question needs 'do'.

quiz.q: I wish I ___ so much money last weekend.
If only I ___ to your advice!
I'm so tired. I should ___ to bed earlier.
She regrets ___ the job in London.
I wish I ___ more free time now.

grammar.title: Weak forms and contractions in past conditionals
grammar.explain: In fast speech, 'have' in 'would have' is weak and sounds like /əv/, so 'would have' sounds like 'would've' /ˈwʊdəv/. 'Had not' becomes 'hadn't' and 'would not' becomes 'wouldn't'.
grammar.explain_ar: في الكلام السريع تُنطق have في would have ضعيفة مثل /əv/، فتُصبح would have مثل would've. وتُختصر had not إلى hadn't و would not إلى wouldn't.

examples.en: I still would've done the same thing.
I wouldn't have made the same decision.
If I hadn't left the UK...
If I'd known, I would've helped.
examples.note: Here I'd = I had (not I would).

mistakes.wrong: I would of done the same.
mistakes.right: I would have (would've) done the same.
mistakes.why: It sounds like 'of', but we write 'have' or 've.
In the if-part, I'd = I had.

quiz.q: How do we usually say 'have' in 'should have gone'?
quiz.why: 'Have' is a weak form in fast speech.
